brief_changes: Added defect item 19: a REF- id alone never grounds origin=sourced (the validator now errors 'reference-only citation'), even though the rule was already stated in the schema's field description and in the brief's own Reference example section - it still recurred in three rows across two skills in one small batch (C11R-002); grep every row whose sources is REF- only before calling a skill done.

Added defect item 20: a composition's claim that it reuses a cited skill's operation 'unchanged' or its vocabulary 'verbatim' is a claim to diff against the actual enum, not a fact the citation proves by itself - compose-improvement-loop claimed compose-loop's terminated_by vocabulary verbatim while declaring a value neither enum contained (C11R-001, block), making its definition_of_done's expected output unreachable from the contract.

Sharpened item 8 with the recurrence found here: a fix landing on the skills a finding names does not clear the pattern from every skill that shares it - xc-tenancy repeated the identical T1-vs-T6.2 gap the sibling xc ceremony had just fixed in four other skills, because it was not in that batch (C11R-003). Sweep siblings at the same layer for a known pattern, not only the skills the finding names.

Updated the defect and what-worked headers to name ceremony 11's three fan-out groups (compose, xc, round2) and folded round2's 96/178-row quote-verification result into the existing quote bullet. Held the brief at 116 lines against the 120-line cap.

metrics_after.full_repo_validate: 100 skills checked, 0 errors, 37 warnings (all pre-existing, none naming the six skills in this batch)

lessons_for_next_section: A skill can claim to reuse a cited skill's vocabulary 'verbatim' and be wrong: compose-improvement-loop's CandidateOutcome.reason enum declared a fourth value compose-loop's terminated_by enum does not carry, and its own instructions never produced it - the definition_of_done's expected output was unreachable from the contract it claimed to build on. A 'reused unchanged'/'verbatim' claim is a promise to diff, not a fact the citation proves by itself.

The schemas/skill.schema.json field description for sources already states the REF-only rule in the exact words the validator now enforces as an error, and the brief already restated it; it still recurred in three rows across two skills in one small batch. A rule stated twice does not stay applied without a check - the validator error is what actually closed it.

The same T1-vs-T6.2 four-entries gap the sibling xc ceremony had just fixed in four skills (C11X-001) recurred in xc-tenancy, a fifth skill carrying the identical shape that was not in that batch. A finding's fix reaching the skills it names does not clear the pattern from every skill that shares it.

Widening a shape to a fourth, schedule-actor worked example is cheapest when a sibling ceremony already built one: xc-tenancy's fourth ScopeByWayIn example reused xc-compensation's own fourth worked example's wording (subject schedule:*, a note naming the T6.2 door and whether it starts or steers, REF-3-4-10 cited directly) almost verbatim rather than being re-derived from scratch.
